chapter: On the road with Victor Spencer
title: The warning not to go and Evan Thomas's death
summary: He was warned away from the place where Thomas was killed and describes him.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But you didn't tell me what happened to Evanne.

Oh, Evanne was playing, you see. You weren't with him that time? No, I was in Crowley. You were close by, huh? Seven miles from there. Yeah. And Evanne was with some woman by the name of Mabel or something, this particular woman's husband had been in penitentiary, and the same day he got out of penitentiary, you understand me, he'd come up on the bandstand and joked him. But old man Ney, his son used to play like Son Johnson but he looked like Gilbert Young. Well he came around that because he used to.

like me telling me don't go over there, because a man woke up in his sleep and told us don't go over there, but God, I think a lot of them was over there, but I don't know, but I didn't go, you understand?
Well this was the floor walker telling you not to go.
Yeah, oh he was a barber too. He was a town barber and he had a son played in his, but what he liked me, because his son Buster thought so much of me, you know, like me.
But being the floor walker he'd know who was talking every time.

But he wasn't a floor walker of rain, he lived in the crowd. But he got up just like around the corner and come around here and tell me, say don't go over there tonight, because this particular guy that committed the crime just had got out of jail and knew that, see, Evanne, daddy was one of them old old doctors. He had a lot of little funny houses painted, white trim with blue and it looked like he took blue and made it to blue, you understand? And Evanne had a really nice place. He had went to Tuskegee, he was highly educated. He went to Tuskegee to learn how to, he was a tailor, you understand? He was a little dog father, he played up some trumpet, he was a high note man, you understand what I mean? And those people used to go for musicians then. See all them bands from Baton Rouge and stuff used to come through there, Dimes and all those bands used to come through those places. Well it would be that, see we'd get our kicks. Now this band with Victor Spencer, what I was in, they had Bunk playing trumpet, they had Bunk playing trumpet, Icy was playing bass, and this boy I told you a while ago was playing piano, Al Greta. And Blake used to be with the Sonny South band, he was from here.
